training_reference: The separately running pristine k16 replication, only if measured and matching controls
hypothesis: Near this fixed ordered FePt reference, a tetragonal crystal-field response dominates an isotropic volume/bandwidth response: |dK/dlog(c/a)| > |dK/dlog(V)| and dK/dlog(c/a) < 0.
hypothesis_status: Prospective hypothesis motivated by the old confounded c-strain response; not a result of electronic SOC matrix-element analysis.
alternatives: Mixed volume-shape interaction invalidates additive response
Sampling or basis dependence dominates the apparent response
model: Additive quadratic K0+A*v+B*s+C*v^2+D*s^2, fit separately to E and F anisotropy with v=log(V/V0), s=log((c/a)/(c/a)0). Fit remains unchanged if the dominance hypothesis fails.
baselines: Constant mean of the same five training measurements
Least-squares quadratic in s only, using the same five training measurements
Least-squares quadratic in v only, using the same five training measurements
heldout_protocol: Do not run mixed-minus/plus until all five training outcomes are collected, the model and baseline predictions are committed and notebook prediction events exist. New +/-0.25% c strains; old +/-0.5% outcomes were already known and are not reused as blind tests.
evaluation: MAE and RMSE across both held-out structures for each model, reported separately for E and F. Response-direction correctness relative to the measured same-runtime reference. No significance or physical-accuracy claim without additional numerical controls.
qualification: Exploratory at fixed k16/DZP/PBE/300 K settings; global convergence checks remain separate. No orbital mechanism established by geometric response alone.

references.role: Primary work identifies important Pt SOC contributions; does not prove our strain-response hypothesis.
Primary convergence/SOC study motivates independent numerical controls; its different functional and basis are not a calibration target.
